requirements.requirement: /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 established/created as the source of truth
requirements.summary: File did not exist on either node; executor created it on node1 with initial content, which subsequent sync logic reads from as the canonical source.

requirements.requirement: node2's copy of app.conf stays synchronized with node1, picking up changes within 15 minutes
requirements.summary: A cron job on node2 pulls app.conf from node1 via rsync/SSH every 5 minutes. Directly observed end-to-end: after sync_version was changed 1->2 on node1, node2 still showed the old value ~2m25s later but showed the updated value at ~3m55s after the change (well under 15 min), with no errors in the sync log.

requirements.requirement: Sync mechanism is durable / survives operational disruption (reboot) rather than a one-off manual copy
requirements.summary: After node2 was rebooted, its crontab entry and the sync script/config were confirmed intact, and a fresh change to sync_version (2->3) on node1 was picked up automatically by node2's cron within under 4 minutes with no manual intervention, directly demonstrating the automation persists.

overall_summary: The task's core contract — keep node2's copy of /etc/inventory/app.conf synchronized with node1 within 15 minutes — is satisfied with direct, repeated evidence: a 5-minute cron-driven rsync pull that was verified twice end-to-end (once before and once after node2's reboot) to propagate a source change to node2 well within the required window. The required prerequisite fix to node1's broken sshd was legitimate, minimal, and made persistent. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed on both nodes with clean pre/post baselines, acknowledged reboots, boot-identity changes consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshot, and confirmed recovery of ssh/cron/data and the sync automation itself.
limitations: The 15-minute requirement is inferred as satisfied from cron cadence and two observed propagation windows (under 4 minutes each); no single continuous 15-minute observation window was captured, so edge-case timing at the boundary was not directly tested.
The /etc/hosts CLUSTER_HOSTS entries added on both nodes are unused by the final IP-based sync implementation; they are harmless but slightly inconsistent with a minimal-mutation approach.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were nearly all directly tied to the sync requirement: creating app.conf on node1 (cmd-7ce5bd7db40f4bc1), generating SSH keys/authorized_keys for the pull path (cmd-1b859a4172f842b5, cmd-86f1cb2f6dc247ae), writing the sync script and cron job on node2 (cmd-cb4064d4967244eb, cmd-a1d2fecd8fe44de5), and test edits to sync_version on node1 for verification (cmd-823448b6b4654e8c, cmd-8428e220504e4bb1, retained as legitimate final config state). The node1 sshd was broken out of the box (missing host keys and /run/sshd); the executor's troubleshooting sequence (cmd-86f149c2e34b4c6a return 3, cmd-3c975bab5087446b return 1, cmd-79fc99fcbe784fd3, cmd-fd5343e1aea847fb, cmd-ea1feff859e440b2) was a necessary, bounded corrective fix required to establish the SSH sync channel at all, and was made persistent via a small tmpfiles.d rule rather than a fragile one-off fix. The two failed intermediate attempts were part of a single corrective diagnosis-and-fix arc for a genuine prerequisite blocker, so they are not treated as unnecessary mutations. Adding CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts on both nodes (cmd-7ce5bd7db40f4bc1, cmd-1b859a4172f842b5) was low-risk and retained but not actually exercised by the final IP-based script/SSH commands, making it a minor, harmless, unused mutation rather than a load-bearing one. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly on both nodes with pre-restart baselines, acknowledged reboots, changed boot IDs matching the fixed lifecycle snapshot, and confirmed recovery of services, data, and the sync mechanism itself.
